overview: Both are glands that secrete substances, but only one uses ducts to deliver its product.
genZNote: Endocrine glands text their hormones straight into the bloodstream. Exocrine glands mail their product through a duct.

aspects.label: Presence of Ducts
aspects.valueA: Ductless — secretions are released directly into the bloodstream.
aspects.valueB: Have ducts that carry secretions to a specific surface or cavity.

aspects.label: What They Secrete
aspects.valueB: Enzymes, sweat, saliva, mucus, and other non-hormonal secretions.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Thyroid gland, adrenal gland, pituitary gland.
aspects.valueB: Salivary glands, sweat glands, sebaceous glands, pancreas (exocrine part).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The pancreas is a classic 'mixed gland' example — it's exocrine (digestive enzymes via a duct) and endocrine (insulin/glucagon into blood) at the same time.
overlay.memoryTrick: Exo = exit through a duct. Endo = enters bloodstream internally, no duct.
overlay.commonMisconception: Endocrine glands are not the only sources of hormones released into blood — some exocrine-associated organs, like the pancreas, also have endocrine components.
